descriptions.shortDescription: Drag-and-drop dashboards with templates, tiles and smart visibility for Nextcloud.
descriptions.longDescription: LaunchPad extends the Nextcloud dashboard. Users create personal workspaces with drag-and-drop widgets, custom shortcut tiles and smart visibility rules, and admins roll out dashboard templates to entire teams. LaunchPad works with every existing Nextcloud dashboard widget, supporting both the v1 and v2 Dashboard APIs. It suits organisations that want consistent, curated dashboards for their teams while still giving users the freedom to personalise them. Conduction maintains this component within the Nextcloud ISV programme. LaunchPad is available in the Nextcloud App Store at https://apps.nextcloud.com/apps/launchpad.
features: Drag-and-drop grid layout to position and resize widgets
Multiple dashboards per user
Custom shortcut tiles with icons, colours and links
Admin templates distributed to user groups
View-only, add-only or full customisation per template
Conditional widget visibility by group, time of day or date
Per-widget styling of colours, borders and titles
Compulsory widgets that users cannot remove
Dashboard sharing with users, groups or a read-only public link
Group dashboards next to personal dashboards

descriptions.shortDescription: Drag-and-drop dashboards met templates, tegels en slimme zichtbaarheid voor Nextcloud.
descriptions.longDescription: LaunchPad breidt het Nextcloud-dashboard uit. Gebruikers maken persoonlijke werkruimtes met drag-and-drop widgets, eigen snelkoppelingstegels en slimme zichtbaarheidsregels, en beheerders rollen dashboardtemplates uit naar hele teams. LaunchPad werkt met elke bestaande Nextcloud-dashboardwidget en ondersteunt zowel de v1- als de v2-Dashboard-API. Het is bedoeld voor organisaties die consistente, samengestelde dashboards voor hun teams willen, terwijl gebruikers de vrijheid houden om ze te personaliseren. Conduction onderhoudt dit component binnen het Nextcloud ISV-programma. LaunchPad is beschikbaar in de Nextcloud App Store via https://apps.nextcloud.com/apps/launchpad.
features: Drag-and-drop rasterindeling om widgets te plaatsen en te schalen
Meerdere dashboards per gebruiker
Eigen snelkoppelingstegels met iconen, kleuren en links
Beheerdertemplates die naar gebruikersgroepen worden uitgerold
Alleen bekijken, toevoegen of volledige aanpassing per template
Conditionele zichtbaarheid van widgets op groep, tijdstip of datum
Styling per widget voor kleuren, randen en titels
Verplichte widgets die gebruikers niet kunnen verwijderen
Dashboards delen met gebruikers, groepen of via een alleen-lezen publieke link
Groepsdashboards naast persoonlijke dashboards

Their organisation is the domain of their address, or for a personal, hidden or noreply address the company on their public profile. The owning organisation (conduction.nl) is the most common organisation domain, the domains and names in publiccode.yml and the owner account; one person with two addresses counts twice. Bots are left out.

results.title: Project health (CHAOSS)
results.description: How active and widely carried the project is: the bus factor, the spread over organisations, how change requests and issues are handled, and how often it releases. Informative: shown, not rated.
results.message: 6 of 6 CHAOSS metrics measured. They are shown for information and do not count in any rating.

metrics.name: Contributor Absence Factor
metrics.explanation: The fewest people who together made half of the commits on the default branch in the last 12 months, of the 100 contributors GitHub reports, among 8 human contributors. At 1 the project depends on a single person. Bots are left out; one person with several accounts or addresses counts more than once.

metrics.name: Organizational Diversity
metrics.explanation: Organisations are told apart by the email domain of the latest 300 commits of the last 12 months (254 commits by people, after the .mailmap) and, for a personal or hidden address, by the company on the author's public profile. The largest is conduction.nl (6 authors), with 100% of the 254 commits whose organisation is known; 0% of the commits come from 0 of 6 authors whose organisation stays unknown. Only these counts are kept, no names, addresses or companies; an organisation is named only when several authors share it.

metrics.name: Change Request Closure Ratio
metrics.explanation: 1,011 change requests were closed (merged or not) and 1,040 opened in the last 90 days, bots included. Below 1 the open backlog grows; above 1 it shrinks.

metrics.name: Time to First Response
metrics.explanation: None of the 15 latest change requests opened by people between 2026-08-23 and 2026-11-14 got a comment or review from anyone but its author.

metrics.name: Issue Response Time
metrics.explanation: None of the 5 latest issues opened by people between 2026-08-23 and 2026-11-14 got a comment from anyone but its author.

metrics.name: Release Frequency
metrics.explanation: 8 final releases were published in the last 12 months, about one every 46 days, counted from the GitHub releases. The latest final release is from 2026-09-06. Besides these, 269 pre-releases were published; they are not counted. Drafts and pre-releases are left out.

openBreaches.title: Pre-existing hydra gate failures on development (6 gates)
Legacy @spec tags point at archived change dirs (~253 unresolved gate-46 anchors)
Suppression & baseline audit: what the green PHPMD number hides
Hydra Gates were dead (pin missing gate script paths); with the pin removed, 9 real gate findings surface
gate-57: the GroupFolder dashboard-content backend (REQ-GFSB-001) receives no reads, writes or deletes
gate-19's covered half is mostly illusory: 108 of 117 @e2e anchors point at tests CI never runs (4 of ~107 execute)
groupfolder-storage-backend is unreachable: read/write/delete all have zero callers, while migrate --prune-source already NULLs the DB column
Question: Availability on Nextcloud App Store
First full e2e execution: 15 of 80 root-suite tests fail — including a non-admin Create CTA that answers 400
gate-26: the admin templates page has no CI e2e coverage, and its only 'test' targets a data-testid that does not exist
dashboard-kiosk-mode: 23 spec scenarios are unsatisfiable — the kiosk frontend was removed in 1fd075c5, backend still routed
runtime-shell REQ-SHELL-003 describes a toolbar removed in 18d601a0 — and its two sibling scenarios were @e2e-excluded without noticing
No conditional-visibility EXCLUDE rule can be created: isInclude=false is a boolean bound into a smallint column (400 on PostgreSQL = the CI default)
conditional-visibility editor: the group picker is always empty — Views.vue never passes available-groups, so group rules cannot be built or previewed in the UI
Conditional visibility is never enforced: checkRulesForPlacement() has no render-time caller, so preview says Hidden and the dashboard shows the widget anyway
spec(grid-layout): the "Placement key regeneration" scenario mandates a WCAG 2.1.1 regression, and is filed under "Grid Styling"
spec(dashboards): two different requirements share the id REQ-DASH-015, so any #req-dash-015 anchor is ambiguous
filterDashboards() would blank every result — extractUuid() probes a magic accessor on launchpad's own Dashboard entity (latent: no callers yet)
stylelint lints 31 of 82 .vue files — the globs are unquoted, so POSIX sh expands them one level deep
clock-weather-widgets: the clock and weather requirements share two scenario titles, collapsing four scenarios to two addressable slugs

notes: Measured over the open issues and the issues closed in the last 90 days, in working days (Monday to Friday, Europe/Amsterdam, without Dutch public holidays).
Only the 200 most recently updated issues of each kind were read.

Vulnerabilities are read from the published GitHub security advisories, from draft to publication. Their response time, unpublished advisories and Dependabot alerts need admin rights and are not measured.
No issue carries a blocking label (such as blocker or critical), so every bug counts as an other bug.
